'''Rahmat Ali Rahmat''' (1891 – 7 April 1963) was an Indian educator, poet, and author associated with Urdu and Odia literature. He was a prominent mathematics teacher in Odisha and also wrote Urdu poetry characterized by elements of mysticism, humour, and social satire.

== Early life and education ==
Rahmat Ali Rahmat was born in 1891 in Rasulpur, [[Cuttack district]], [[Bengal Presidency]] (now in [[Odisha]]).<ref>{{cite book |last1=Newalpuri|first1=Hafizullah|author-link1=Hafizullah Newalpuri|title=Orissa Mein Urdu|trans-title=Urdu In Orissa|publisher=[[National Council for Promotion of Urdu Language]] |location= [[New Delhi]]|date= 2001 |hdl= |url=https://www.rekhta.org/ebooks/odisha-mein-urdu-hafeezullah-newalpuri-ebooks#162 |page=160 |language=ur}}</ref>
He received his early education in Urdu, Persian, and mathematics from his elder brother, Irfan Ali Fidai. After completing schooling at [[Ravenshaw Collegiate School]], Cuttack (1908–1912), he passed the [[matriculation]] under [[University of Calcutta]] in 1912, the [[Intermediate of Arts|F.A.]] in 1914, and graduated in 1916. He completed his [[Licentiate (degree)|Licentiate]] in Training (L.T.) in 1918. During his school years, he was a contemporary and friend of [[Subhas Chandra Bose]].<ref>{{cite book|editor1-last=Naqeeb|editor1-first=Khawar|editor1-link=Khawar Naqeeb|title=Bayāz e Rahmat (A poetry collection of Rahmat Ali Rahmat [1891–1963])|url=https://www.rekhta.org/ebooks/detail/bayaz-e-rahmat-rahmat-ali-rahmat-ebooks#13 |edition=1st|year=2014|location =[[Delhi]]|publisher=Educational Publishing House|language=ur|page=12}}</ref>{{Sfn|Newalpuri|2001|p=160}}

== Career ==
After completing his L.T. in 1918, Rahmat began teaching at Muslim Seminary School (now [[Sayeed Seminary]]) in 1919. In 1920, he entered government service and taught in various district schools, including [[Sambalpur]] and [[Puri (city)|Puri]]. By 1935, he was appointed Headmaster of the Practising Middle School, Cuttack. Later, he was promoted as Special Inspecting Officer for Mohammedan Education (1943) and served as District Inspector of Schools (D.I.) in [[Balasore]] and [[Ganjam]] Plains until his retirement in May 1950.{{Sfn|Naqeeb|2014|pp=12–13}}{{Sfn|Newalpuri|2001|pp=160–161}}

His notable students include [[Sachidananda Routray]], Hrudananda Ray, Rajkishore Ray, Gobinda Chandra Udgata, [[Nandini Satpathy]], [[Surendranath Dwivedy]], Sheikh Habibullah, and Sheikh Inayatullah.{{Sfn|Naqeeb|2014|p=13}}

== Literary works ==
Rahmat wrote several mathematics textbooks in [[Odia language|Odia]] and English, which remained in the Odisha school curriculum for about four decades (1936–1976). These included ''Ganit Sopan'', ''Probeshika Ganit Sopan'', ''Bijoganit Sopan'', ''Jyamiti Sopan'', ''Man Sankha Mala'', and ''Beauties of Algebra'' (1952).{{Sfn|Naqeeb|2014|p=13}}

He also authored ''Jawahar al-Qawaid'', an Urdu grammar book, and translated [[Deputy Nazir Ahmad]]’s ''Taubat-un-Nasuh'' into Odia, which remains unpublished.<ref name="Aab-e-Khizar">{{cite book |last=Karamat |first=Karamat Ali|author-link=Karamat Ali Karamat|title=Aab-e-Khizr: Shora-e-Odisa ka Intikhab-e-Kalam ma'a Tazkira |trans-title=Elixir of Life: Selected Works and Biographical Notes of Odisha's Poets|url=https://www.rekhta.org/ebooks/aab-e-khizr-shora-e-odisa-ka-intikhab-e-kalam-ma-tazkira-ebooks#168 |location=Cuttack |publisher=Odisha Urdu Publishers |date=August 1963 |language=ur |page=167}}</ref>

Rahmat's poetry reflects elements of Sufism, humour, and philosophical critique. Although influenced by [[Akbar Allahabadi]] and [[Deputy Nazir Ahmad]], his works exhibit originality in tone and diction.{{Sfn|Newalpuri|2001|pp=167–171}}

The book ''Cuttack, One Thousand Years'' mentions him among notable 20th-century Urdu writers and poets from Odisha.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Behera |first1=Karuna Sagar |last2=Paṭṭanāẏaka |first2=Jagannātha | last3=Das|first3=H. C. |title=Cuttack, One Thousand Years |url=https://books.google.com/books/about/Cuttack_One_Thousand_Years.html?id=JRVuAAAAMAAJ |date=1990|volume=2|publisher=Cuttack City Millennium Celebrations Committee, The Universe |location=[[Cuttack]] |page=14|language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Rahmat married twice. His first wife, Hajra Begum of Dariapur, Sungra, bore him one son and two daughters, of whom only Umm-e-Salam survived childhood. His second wife, Waziran Begum, was the daughter of Muhammad Ismail Khan of Talpatk. They had three sons and five daughters, including [[Karamat Ali Karamat]], who became a noted Urdu poet and writer.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Rahman |first1=Azizur|last2=Jāmi|first2=Abdul Matīn|author-link2=Abdul Mateen Jami|title=Urdu Adab Ka Koh e Noor Karāmat Alī Karāmat|url=https://www.rekhta.org/ebooks/detail/urdu-adab-ka-koh-e-noor-karamat-ali-karamat-abdul-matin-jami-ebooks|date=2022 |publisher=[[Odisha Urdu Academy]]|location=Bhubaneswar|language=ur|pages=29–30}}</ref>

== Death and legacy ==
Rahmat Ali Rahmat died on 7 April 1963 and was buried near Azan Gah in the precincts of [[Qadam e Rasool, Cuttack|Qadam Rasool]], Cuttack.{{Sfn|Naqeeb|2014|pp=12–13}}{{Sfn|Newalpuri|2001|pp=160–161}}

Rahmat’s contribution to education and Urdu literature in Odisha is recognized in several Urdu literary anthologies. [[Malik Ram]] noted that [[Amjad Najmi]] had benefited from Rahmat’s scholarship.<ref name="malik">{{cite journal|last=Ram|first=Malik|author-link=Malik Ram|title=Deaths: Amjad Najmi, Muhammad Amjad, Shaikh|url=https://www.rekhta.org/ebooks/tahreer-delhi-shumara-number-004-malik-ram-magazines-16#59 |journal=Tahreer|volume=8|issue=4|date=October–December 1974|publisher=Daftar-e-Ilmi Majlis|location=Delhi|page=59|language=ur}}</ref> In his autobiographical account, Najmi himself wrote that Rahmat was known as a distinguished teacher of both mathematics and Urdu literature. He mentioned that Rahmat authored an Urdu grammar book titled ''Jawahar al-Qawaid'', written in a conversational style, which became widely popular soon after publication. Najmi described him as simple, modest, and deeply fond of the prose of [[Deputy Nazir Ahmad]], the language of [[Daagh Dehlvi]], and the humour of [[Akbar Allahabadi]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.rekhta.org/ebooks/aaj-kal-aur-ghubar-e-karwan-khud-navisht-sawanih-ebooks#189 |title=Aaj Kal Aur Ghubār-e-Kārawān (A collection of autobiographies published in the monthly magazine Aaj Kal under the title Ghubār-e-Kārawān) |publisher=Publications Division, Ministry of Information and Communications, [[Government of India]] |year=2000 |isbn=978-81-230-0829-5 |editor-last=Farooqui |editor-first=Mahbubur Rahman |page=182 |language=ur |editor-last2=Kāẓim |editor-first2=Muḥammad}}</ref>  
He is also mentioned in ''Odisha Mein Urdu Shayari'' by Saeed Rahmani for his mastery of mathematics and humour in Urdu poetry.<ref name="Rahmani1">{{cite book |last=Rahmani |first=Saeed |title=Odisha mein Urdu Shayari (Tazkira) |url=https://www.rekhta.org/ebooks/detail/odisha-mein-urdu-shairi-saeed-rahmani-ebooks#23 |date=2018 |publisher=[[Odisha Urdu Academy]] |location=Bhubaneswar |language=ur |page=22}}</ref>
